main_text.p: Caussarum eorundem locupletissimum prom-ptuarium Φυσιολογικὴ & Υγιεινὴ[?] subministrant.
Continenté vero caussam in Morbis nullam esse: in Ægris haud diffiteor.
Morbos contractos ab Aere vitioso, longè deteri-ores esse censeo, quàm vel à cibo aut potu itidem prauo.
Symptomatibus nullam deberi, nullamq; postu-lare curationem; eademq; summè perterrefacere sæ-pissimè Medicos, mirandum est. Galenus 12.Method.I.
Dolor est sensatio tristis in sensu tactus, à qualita-tib. ἀθρόως ἢ βιαίως[?] in sensoriū agentibus dependens. Galen.2.de loc.aff.c.2.
Menstrua purgatio ex omnibus hæmorrhagijs sola præternaturalis non existit. Galen.lib.3. de sympt. caus.
Ast Semeioticæ eximia in universa arte necessitas & præstantia existit. quod cum etiam animadver-tisset Hippocrates, scimus quid in eadem operę & studij posuerit.

Solitus est dicere Galenus, perarduum esse Medi-co, ægris absentibus tuto consulere; cum ipse Medi-cus complura ex facie & tactu corporis, affectuum ar-gumenta capiat, quàm vel ex urinis deprehendere pos-sint. In Consilio pro puero Epileptico.

page.notes: Greek words are copied as far as legible: "Φυσιολογικὴ" and "Υγιεινὴ" and "ἀθρόως ἢ βιαίως" are uncertain in accents and some letters, so they are marked [?]. "Method.I." may be "Method.1.". The Roman numeral "XXXIIX." is printed as shown. The catchword "Vt" at the lower right is read as a catchword, not a signature. No page number or running head is printed.
